Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Burch was injured while helping on kickoff coverage in the first quarter. He had a noticeable limp as he left the field and won't be able to return to the contest. Burch had played at least one-third of Arizona's defensive snaps in all but one game coming into Sunday, so his absence will impact Arizona beyond his special-teams contributions.

Williams will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a knee injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Chiefs on Nov. 22. Josh Fryar will likely start at left tackle in Williams' absence.

Minshew incredibly played through the injury in Week 9, logging all 53 offensive snaps and completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in his first start replacing the since-departed Jacoby Brissett. Schefter added that Minshew still is determining the timing of the procedure, but he plans on having it. With Minshew out for the rest of the campaign, rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is taking over under center for the Cardinals.

Carter will remain on IR for Week 10 and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Rams. The defensive tackle logged three consecutive limited practices after being designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Before his departure late in the fourth quarter, London recorded six catches (on 12 targets) for 109 yards. If he's diagnosed with a concussion, he'll be subject to league protocol in order to gain clearance to play again, but the Falcons are on bye in Week 11, so he'll have plenty of time to recover for a Week 12 road matchup with the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Deablo suffered a forearm injury in Week 6 against Chicago and missed Atlanta's subsequent two games. He returned to face the Bengals last Sunday but apparently aggravated the issue, and he didn't practice Thursday or Friday this week. With Deablo now ruled out against the Chiefs, Harold Perkins should get a healthy dose of defensive snaps at linebacker.

Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Randall has been on injured reserve all season while recovering from a neck injury. He was designated to return Oct. 28 but wasn't activated for Week 8 or Week 9. Randall was a fifth-round selection in April's NFL Draft, so if he's activated and gets into Monday's Week 10 matchup, it will be his NFL regular-season debut.

Head coach Jesse Minter ruled out the veteran safety for Monday Night Football following Saturday's practice. It will be the fourth consecutive absence for Hawkins, who is recovering from a knee injury, and that means K'Von Wallace will continue to see more snaps in the secondary. Hawkins' next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Panthers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Williams sustained a calf injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. The linebacker logged nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defensed before leaving the game. Rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr will likely finish the remainder of the contest at inside linebacker next to Terrel Bernard.

Alford sustained a concussion attempting to complete a one-handed interception in the endzone during the third quarter. The slot cornerback will not return to the contest, leaving Damar Hamlin and other defensive backs to fulfill his role for the remainder of the contest.

Benford was cleared to play Sunday after recovering from a wrist injury, but he is now dealing with a groin issue which will prevent him from playing for the rest of Week 10. Dee Alford (concussion) has also been ruled out, so the Bills' secondary will lean more heavily on the likes of Jordan Hancock, Maxwell Hairston and Damar Hamlin.

Shavers drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Jets after logging a trio of full practices during Week 10 prep. However, he was not activated from the PUP list before the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline Saturday, so he will have to wait at least one more week before making his 2026 debut. Shavers' next chance to play is Week 11 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Lee drew the questionable tag after a FP-FP-LP practice log during Week 10 prep. However, the rookie fourth-rounder will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury that he picked up in Week 8 against Green Bay. Malcolm DeWalt and Corey Thornton figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Marco Wilson at outside cornerback in the absence of Lee, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Ravens on Nov. 22.

Christensen drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Saints after logging a trio of full practices. However, he's not quite ready to return from a hamstring injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Jackson's 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and he drew the doubtful tag for Sunday's game after logging a trio of limited sessions. He's not quite ready to return from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, and his next opportunity to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

Horn has had a productive NFL career, amassing 196 total tackles (139 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and 10 interceptions across 56 regular-season games over six seasons. He underwent surgery on his quad back in September. However, until Horn is back on the field or there is a more informative update, he should be considered week-to-week.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.
With Stevenson sidelined and Malik Muhammad (toe) inactive, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips will take on more defensive snaps alongside Jaylon Phillips and Kyler Gordon at cornerback for the Bears.

Muhammad was expected to be able to return to action in Week 9, but the cornerback will now be forced to miss a second straight game while nursing a toe injury he suffered in Week 7. In his absence, Josh Blackwell is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities at cornerback behind starters Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson versus the Buccaneers.

Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.
Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Hinton is dealing with an illness and was added to the Bengals' injury report Sunday morning. He's not feeling well enough to be able to play against Pittsburgh. Hinton's absence will lessen Cincinnati's depth on the offensive line.

Risner was a Sunday addition to Cincinnati's injury report due to an illness. He was initially tagged as questionable to play, but he'll ultimately be able to suit up. Risner should assume his regular role as the Bengals' starting right guard.

Iosivas was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Steelers despite logging full practices Thursday and Friday. He'll remain on IR for at least one more game, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.

Davis was placed on injured reserve in late September after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals now have 21 days to officially activate the 30-year-old for him to remain eligible to play this season.

Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Booker was hurt late in the first half Sunday. He was deemed questionable to return and never re-entered the contest. T.J. Bass replaced Booker during Sunday's loss and will likely be called upon to start if Booker needs to miss additional time.

Bland hurt his ankle during Sunday's loss to San Francisco and couldn't finish the game. The issue may be an aggravation of the injury that limited the cornerback in practice Friday. The results of Bland's imaging should provide clarity about whether he's at risk of missing additional time. Cobie Durant would likely slide back into a starting role if Bland does have to sit out any games.

The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.

The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.

Denver Broncos.longComment: After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.
Moss has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Jahdae Barron will likely finish the game at outside cornerback for the Broncos.

Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Hutchinson is expected to undergo more tests on his right knee once the Lions return home from Munich, but it appears the superstar pass rusher could be out of action for quite some time. It's a significant blow for a Detroit defense that has looked far better over the last few weeks, and Hutchinson's pass-rushing prowess has played a big part in that progression. Rookie second-rounder Derrick Moore, DJ Wonnum and Tyler Lacy will all take on larger roles on defense for as long as Hutchinson is sidelined.

Joseph was a full participant in practice Thursday, but it appears the Lions are taking a cautious approach to his return. The 25-year-old has one more chance to return from the reserve/PUP list in Week 11 before he becomes ineligible for the remainder of the season.

Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

Moore suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, and after being evaluated by medical staff, it's been determined that the fifth-year pro will not return to Sunday's contest. With Bo Melton (thigh) also done for the day, the Packers will turn to Savion Williams and Matthew Golden as return options on kickoffs and special teams. Moore is in jeopardy of missing the Packers' next contest, which takes place in Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Cisse picked up the injury during the first quarter, and he's being checked on by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Carrington Valentine, Kamal Hadden and Benjamin St-Juste are candidates for more defensive snaps while Cisse is being evaluated in the locker room.

Zeitler was initially deemed as questionable due to ankle and triceps injuries, which will ultimately prevent him from playing in Sunday's NFC North tilt. His next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Franklin did not participate in Week 10 prep due to a shin injury he suffered in Week 6. The inside linebacker will now miss a fourth consecutive game, leaving Isaiah McDuffie to continue as the starter alongside Ty'Ron Hopper.

Whyle suffered a concussion in Week 8 against Carolina and missed last Sunday's win over the Patriots. He had already been ruled for Sunday's contest against Minnesota before the Packers decided to place him on IR. Whyle didn't log a catch or target during his eight contests before getting hurt, so his blocking and work on special teams will be the primary voids during his absence.

Houston Texans.longComment: Montgomery hasn't suited up since he suffered a groin injury Week 5 in Tennessee. However, he practiced in full for the first time since getting hurt this past Friday, and the Texans described his work during Week 10 prep as a "ramp-up" ahead of potentially returning Week 11. Ryans didn't sound certain after Sunday's loss to Cleveland that Montgomery will be able to play versus the Colts, but if the veteran running back does suit up, it could be a huge boost to a Houston offense that may be without the RB who has been filling in as the starter for Montgomery. Woody Marks suffered a concussion Sunday and isn't likely to be cleared in time to play Thursday.

With the Texans on a short week ahead of the contest, Ryans noted of Marks, "just not enough time for him to turn it around that quickly." As for the Week 11 status of fellow RB David Montgomery (groin) -- who was inactive again Sunday -- Ryans said "I'm not certain if David can play or not," adding "we'll take it one day at a time to see how he feels and how he can get back." Prior to his exit Sunday, Marks had 12 carries for 50 yards and one catch for 15 yards. Meanwhile, Emari Demercado finished up with seven carries for 16 yards and one catch for minus-one yards, while Dare Ogunbowale logged one carry for two yards and one catch for 13 yards.

Teller must miss Sunday's contest due to an illness. The reserve right guard's absence means third-string option Evan Brown will be next up behind Ed Ingram and Febechi Nwaiwu if any members of the Texans' interior offensive line must exit the game.

Smith landed on injured reserve in early October due to a hamstring injury. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Smith would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: Gardner has been working through a calf issue all season, and it appears the injury has cropped up again in Week 10. Charvarius Ward (shin) is also questionable to return, so the Colts will need to rely more heavily on Justin Walley, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris at corner.

Ward sustained the injury in the third quarter and was carted to the locker room, where he's undergoing tests to determine whether he can return. Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken are both in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary for as long as Ward is out of the game.

Raimann took a hit to the head in the first quarter, and following tests by medical staff, the fifth-year offensive lineman has been diagnosed with a concussion. Luke Tenuta will stay in at left tackle for the rest of Sunday's game due to the absence of Raimann, who faces an uphill battle to play in the Colts' Week 11 tilt against the Texans on Thursday Night Football.

Davis-Gaither was already ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami in what would be his second consecutive missed contest due to a knee injury. Now that he's been placed on IR, the seventh-year pro will be required to miss at least four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Alie-Cox was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, and his groin injury is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. That means he'll be required to miss at least four games, and with the Colts on a bye for Week 13, that means the next time Alie-Cox can play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20. Will Mallory (hamstring) has also been ruled out for Week 10, so Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown will serve as the Colts' backup tight ends behind Tyler Warren against Miami.

Mallory was a late addition to the Colts' injury report due to a hamstring issue that cropped up Friday. The fourth-year pro will not be available for Sunday's contest, and with Mo Alie-Cox (groin) placed on injured reserve, Tyler Warren will be backed up by Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown. Mallory's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

"We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Hainsey appeared to injure his knee while blocking on a run play in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. Jonah Monheim has taken over at center in Hainsey's absence.
Striggow has operated in a rotational role on the defensive line, so Bryan Thomas should see a bump in defensive snaps for as long as the former is out of the game.
Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter with an ankle injury. The tight end fractured his ankle and did not return to the contest. The 26-year-old will likely be placed on injured reserve soon as he begins to recover from the injury.
Smith has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Mike Caliendo is set to finish the game at right guard.

Ott drew the questionable tag for Week 10 after popping up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. The injury is severe enough for him to miss Sunday's game, and his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Cardinals on Nov. 22. With both Ott and Kenneth Walker (groin) sidelined, the Chiefs' backfield will be led by rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson, while Nate Carter -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- operates in a rotational role.

Walker showed up at the Chiefs' facilities Friday with a tight groin, didn't take part in the ensuing practice and then was listed as questionable for Week 10 action. The team then ruled him out Saturday, which Rapoport called "more precautionary than anything else." In Walker's absence, rookie fifth-round pick Emmett Johnson is expected to be Kansas City's primary runner.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Bowers was in and out of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks due to an ankle injury before the Raiders eventually ruled him out at the start of the second half. In his minimal work in what was rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza's first career start, Bowers hauled in both of his targets for 18 yards. Monday's testing may provide a firm diagnosis and subsequent prognosis for Bowers.

Paye exited the second half of Sunday's game with a neck injury. The linebacker logged five tackles before departing. Malcolm Koonce will likely finish the game at strongside linebacker opposite Maxx Crosby.

Booker was a full participant in Friday's practice but remained questionable headed into the weekend. The defensive lineman appears to not be quite ready to suit up, leaving JJ Pegues to see more defensive snaps in Sunday's contest.

Thornton was a late addition to the Raiders' injury report due to a back issue. It's been determined by medical staff that the second-year wide receiver will not play in Sunday's contest, and Thornton has yet to play in a regular-season game in 2026 after appearing in 15 contests during his rookie campaign. Dareke Young and Cody White will operate as the depth options at wide receiver behind Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: McConkey's next chance to play will thus arrive Nov. 22 against the Jets. In his absence versus Baltimore, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith will be available to lead Los Angeles' WR corps.

Taylor sat out every Chargers practice this week, so it's not surprising that he's not going to be able to play Monday. The second-year offensive tackle has worked in a rotational role when healthy this season, so his absence will affect the Chargers' depth along the offensive line.

Pipkins hasn't played since Week 1 due to a knee injury. He was placed on IR in late September and had his 21-day practice window opened this past Thursday. The Chargers will need to activate Pipkins from injured reserve in order for him to be eligible to suit up Monday.

Awosika hasn't played since Week 2, when he suffered a leg injury against the Raiders. The 28-year-old managed a full practice Saturday following limited sessions Thursday and Friday, so he has a genuine chance of returning to action Monday. Awosika will likely return to a starting role at left guard if he's able to suit up.

It will be the second straight absence for Williamson after he hurt his calf in Week 8 against the Rams. His absence will be felt on special teams, where he has logged all of his snaps so far this season.

Waxter was hurt in the first quarter last Sunday against Houston and couldn't return to the contest. He was unable to practice at all this week and has thus been ruled out for Monday Night Football. Waxter has played in four games so far this season, logging eight tackles (seven solo) over 44 defensive snaps and 26 snaps on special teams.

Eboigbe hurt his ankle last Sunday against Houston and missed Thursday's practice. He was able to log limited sessions Friday and Saturday, however, to give himself a chance to play Monday. If Eboigbe can't give it a go, Nick Barrett could pick up many of his defensive snaps.

Perryman has missed the entire season to date due to a pectoral injury. He was designated to return Nov. 4 and logged an LP/FP/FP practice progression this week. Perryman would have to be activated from IR in order to make his season debut Monday.

Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: With both Shelton and backup center Dylan McMahon (knee) ruled out, the Rams' offensive line depth has become razor-thin. David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer will likely finish the game at center for the team.

McMahon replaced Coleman Shelton (hamstring) at center after Shelton exited the contest. The backup center has also been ruled out, leaving David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to finish the game at center.

Cardona will end up missing a third consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Jake McQuaide will once again serve as the Rams' long snapper.

Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

After the Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve Thursday, Nacua must miss at least four games, which means his earliest return date is Sunday, Dec. 20 against the Cowboys. Considering the timeline given in Rapoport's report, Nacua thus may miss only the minimum number of contests while on IR after suffering PCL and MCL sprains and also a turf-toe injury last Sunday at Washington. With Davante Adams (hamstring) out at least one more outing, L.A. is rolling with a receiving corps of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley in Week 10.

This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Meyer started Sunday in place of Aaron Brewer, who was unable to suit up due to a concussion. With Meyer now at least temporarily sidelined, Jarrett Kingston has taken over at center for Miami.

Biggers injured his knee late in the first quarter, and medical staff has determined that the second-year defensive tackle's injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Keith Cooper and Kenneth Grant will both see more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Biggers' absence.

The rookie sat out both Thursday and Friday's practices before being given a doubtful designation for Sunday's contest, and his inactive status is now official. With Bell, who'd posted a 7-56-0 line on 10 targets in Weeks 7 and 8 before being blanked against the Lions in Week 9, sitting out Sunday, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert could share No. 3 receiver snaps while working with new starting quarterback Kyle McCord.

Baker was designated to return to practice Wednesday, but he isn't yet ready for game action. The veteran cornerback hasn't yet played for Miami after signing a one-year contract to join the organization last March. Baker's next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Nov. 22, in Buffalo.

With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: It appeared that Van Ginkel sustained his injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Blake Cashman (concussion) is inactive, so Jake Golday is in line for more defensive snaps at linebacker for as long as Van Ginkel is being evaluated by medical staff.

Jones is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. He was a practice squad elevation Saturday to give the Vikings more depth at wide receiver due to the absences of both Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf).

Richter injured his foot in the first quarter, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for the third-year linebacker to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Richter's playing time this season has primarily come on special teams, and his availability for Week 11 against the 49ers on Nov. 22, is up in the air.

A late addition to the Week 10 injury report, Addison took a questionable tag into Sunday after sustaining the thumb injury during Friday's practice. After Addison went through a pregame workout, the Vikings opted to hold him out for Sunday's contest while the thumb issue was seemingly inhibiting him while catching the football. With Addison and top tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist) both sidelined, trade-deadline pickup Kirk Cousins won't have many weapons to work with beyond No. 1 wideout Justin Jefferson in his first start for Minnesota since 2023.

Murray is on the mend from a Grade 2 hamstring injury, which he sustained during the Vikings' Week 8 loss to the Lions. The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and the veteran quarterback will take over as the team's new starter beginning with Sunday's game at Green Bay, with Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer working as the reserve options behind him. Once he overcomes the hamstring injury, Murray will look to wrest the No. 2 job away from Wentz.

New England Patriots.longComment: After exiting Sunday's loss to the Lions with an ankle injury, Maye now appears likely to miss additional time beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye. His status for New England's next game against the Chargers is thus in doubt pending the results of the additional testing. Tommy DeVito entered in relief of Maye against Detroit and was ineffective, competing just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, one touchdown and an interception. New England appears to be in big trouble on offense.

Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday in Munich, Germany. However, the veteran wideout suffered a hamstring injury while making a catch in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the defeat, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is once we get back and kind of go from there." New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays, which will be Sunday, Nov. 29, against the Chargers.

Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

Schooler missed the first four games of the season due to a back injury, and he now will sit out a fifth due to the hamstring issue that forced him out of a Week 9 loss to the Packers. The Patriots likely will turn to some combination of Mike Brown and Jaylen Reed to cover Schooler's typical special-teams duties.

Rouse entered concussion protocol following last Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers and was a non-participant in practice to begin Week 10 prep. He was able to close the week with a pair of limited practices en route to taking a questionable tag into Sunday, but Rouse apparently wasn't able to clear the five-step protocol in advance of game day.

Henderson was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, and now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. Henderson's next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Chiefs on Monday, Dec. 21, although there's no timetable for his return, as he is recovering from "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of neurological symptoms." If Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) cannot play Sunday, then the Patriots' backfield will be led by Corey Kiner and Lan Larison.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Richards suffered a knee injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Mason Murphy has taken over at right tackle in Richards' absence.

Werner left in the first half due to a hamstring injury, which medical staff has deemed severe enough for the sixth-year linebacker to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Danny Stutsman will work alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker in the absence of Werner, whose status for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, is up in the air.

Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

New York Giants.longComment: Pinnock exited the game early in the third quarter with a back injury, and his status for the rest of the game is uncertain. In his absence, Tyler Nubin will be thrust into a more prominent role in New York's secondary.

Harrison was limited at practice throughout the week and has since been ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with the Commanders. The 28-year-old has played sparingly on defense during the 2026 campaign, though his absence will be felt on special teams. Harrison's next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 11 versus Jacksonville.

New York Jets.longComment: Smith was hurt during New York's final offensive series of the first half Sunday when he was hit by a pair of defenders while throwing an incomplete pass. He was placed in concussion protocol and passed, clearing the way for him to return to the game. However, Smith then exited again after hurting his ankle, and this time he was unable to return. The veteran quarterback's practice activity, if any, during Week 11 prep will likely determine if he's able to suit up next Sunday against the Chargers. If Smith can't play, rookie Cade Klubnik would likely start behind center.

After being deemed questionable to return to the contest earlier Sunday, Cooper has now been ruled out and will target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Chargers. In his absence versus Buffalo, Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams are available lead New York's WR corps.
Parham exited the second quarter of Sunday's game with a knee injury. Jordan Meredith is set to fill in at left guard while Parham is absent.

Brownlee developed an illness during Week 10 prep, and he will be an observer for Sunday's contest after not being cleared by medical staff to play. D'Angelo Ponds should take on a larger role in the Jets' secondary in the absence of Brownlee, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Elliott dealt with an ankle issue during Week 10 prep but was initially cleared to suit up Sunday. However, he's now dealing with a knee injury that occurred during pregame warmups. Elliott's loss is a blow to Pittsburgh's secondary, though he's played in only two games so far this season. Robert Spears-Jennings figures to take on a large defensive snap share Sunday in Elliott's stead.

Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: Evans is missing his third consecutive game this Sunday in Dallas due to right Achilles tendinitis that he suffered during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. He hasn't practiced in the meantime, and while he's a rare player who doesn't need on-field reps during the week to be available on game days, he would provide confidence in his ability to play again with an appearance in drills at some point this Wednesday through Friday.

West has been on IR since Sept. 23 due to a knee injury. He upgraded to a full practice session Friday after being limited Wednesday and Thursday, but the 49ers aren't yet ready to activate him. Prior to getting hurt, West logged action in two games, recording five tackles (one solo) over 49 defensive snaps and five special-teams snaps.

Hobbs had his 21-day practice window opened Nov. 4, so the 49ers still have ample time to activate him before he'd need to miss the rest of the season. The veteran cornerback hasn't yet made his regular-season San Francisco debut after signing with the team on a one-year contract last March. Hobbs did manage to log a trio of full practices this week, so he seems to be progressing well toward a return to action.

Halton will be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season, but the rookie fourth-rounder is expected to be back for OTAs in May. He'll end his first NFL campaign with 15 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and a scoop-and-score across eight regular-season games.

In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Lucas was hurt during the first quarter and was unable to return. Head coach Mike Macdonald said after the victory that the team isn't sure of the severity of the issue, so Lucas could be headed for imaging. Charles Cross (ankle) missed Sunday's matchup, so Josh Jones and Bobby Hart ended up finishing the game as the Seahawks' offensive tackles. Seattle is on bye Week 11, though it's unclear if that will give Lucas and/or Cross enough time to recover.

Holani exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with a knee injury. The running back will not return, leaving another player to fill his special teams role as Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet continue to dominate the Seahawks' running game.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: While Tampa Bay has been on bye for Week 10, Mayfield has been in and out of a walking boot in recent days in an attempt to rehab the injury, per Garafolo. Though the injury isn't viewed as a long-term concern and a stint on injured reserve isn't in consideration, Mayfield could still be at risk of missing his fourth game of the season in Week 11, after he was sidelined from Weeks 4 through 6 due to a dislocated right thumb. Mayfield has struggled since returning from that injury, completing 25 of 46 pass attempts (54.3 percent) for 307 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while the Buccaneers have embraced a run-heavy attack.

While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Winfield sustained an ankle injury late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. With Winfield unavailable, Ifeatu Melifonwu will continue to operate as one of Tampa Bay's primary safeties versus Chicago.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: The Titans were already without Carnell Tate (shoulder) Sunday, and now,  Robinson's status will need to be monitored ahead of next weekend's game against the Cowboys. Next up for the team's WR snaps/targets should one or both of the aforementioned players be sidelined in Week 11 are Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike.

With Adams done for the day, Terrell Burgess and Isaiah Oliver are both in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary. Adams will need to clear the league's concussion protocol in order to play in Week 11 against the Cowboys on Nov. 22.

Townsend suffered a knee injury during the Week 7 loss to Cleveland and is also now dealing with an Achilles issue. His placement on IR means he'll be sidelined for at least four games. Thomas Morstead was signed by Tennessee from the practice squad to the active roster to take Townsend's role as the team's punter.

Skoronski was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury that he picked up in Week 8 against the Bengals. Now that he's on IR, the fourth-year offensive lineman will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 14 against the Lions on Sunday, Dec. 13. James Hudson and Garrett Dellinger figure to be the top candidates to start at left guard in Skoronski's absence.

In a corresponding transaction, Tennessee activated linebacker Dorian Mausi from injured reserve. Williams won't be able to return to game action until Week 14 against the Lions at the earliest. In the meantime, Mausi figures to assume the small role Williams was occupying.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Patrick suffered a concussion during Sunday's game versus the Rams, and it will keep him out for his third game this season in Week 10. In his absence, rookie sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin figures to take over at center Thursday.

Yankoff did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice after missing Monday with a knee injury. Week 10 will be Washington's first game without the 26-year-old, though the injury is not presumed to be serious. Yankoff has three catches on five targets, for 22 yards through eight games.

Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.
